pair_rules.reason: Historically flagged as incompatible, but modern evidence shows the reaction is minor and mostly a non-issue at typical use pH and concentrations. Formulating at low pH (<5) minimizes any risk.
Retinol prefers near-neutral pH (5.5-6.5) while Ascorbic Acid needs low pH (<4) to stay active. Combining in one phase forces a pH compromise that degrades one or both actives.
Benzoyl Peroxide oxidizes and deactivates Retinol on contact. Do not combine in the same formula or phase.
Both are active exfoliants/actives that increase irritation risk when combined at high concentration; also compete for the same mildly acidic pH window, increasing the chance of barrier disruption.
Both perform best at low pH so they are chemically compatible, but combined acidity can raise irritation risk on sensitive skin.
Common, well-established surfactant pairing; CAPB moderates SLS irritation.
Carbomer gels can be destabilized by electrolytes and by high levels of fatty alcohols if not properly neutralized and phased; use correct mixing order.
Standard neutralization pair; Sodium Hydroxide is commonly used to neutralize Carbomer into a clear gel.
Chelators can interact with mineral UV filter surface coatings in some formulations; verify with the specific coated grade used.
Classic soap-type emulsification pair (TEA-stearate), well characterized in traditional lotion formulation.
Standard, widely used preservative-booster combination that broadens the antimicrobial spectrum.
Both are oxidation-prone; combining can accelerate discoloration/degradation of the formula unless well antioxidant-stabilized.
